claim: Juvenile hormone (JH) induces intestinal stem cell (ISC) driven absorptive epithelial expansion balancing energy uptake with increased energy demands of pregnancy in fruit flies.
source: In fruit flies, juvenile hormone (JH) induces intestinal stem cell (ISC) driven absorptive epithelial expansion balancing energy uptake with increased energy demands of pregnancy.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Reiff et al., 2015) and is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: 20-Hydroxy-Ecdysone (20HE) titer in ovaries and hemolymph are increased upon mating.
source: Upon mating, 20HE titer in ovaries and hemolymph are increased and act on nearby midgut progenitors inducing Ecdysone-induced-protein-75B (Eip75B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C measuring 20HE titers in virgin vs mated females.

claim: The PPARγ-homologue Eip75B drives ISC daughter cells towards absorptive enterocyte lineage ensuring epithelial growth.
source: Strikingly, the PPARγ-homologue Eip75B drives ISC daughter cells towards absorptive enterocyte lineage ensuring epithelial growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figures 3-5 showing forced expression and knockdown experiments of Eip75B isoforms.

claim: This is the first time a systemic hormone is shown to direct local stem cell fate decisions.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first time a systemic hormone is shown to direct local stem cell fate decisions.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the novelty of the findings, based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: Steroid hormones have a protective but mechanistically unclear role in female colorectal cancer patients.
source: Given the protective, but mechanistically unclear role of steroid hormones in female colorectal cancer patients, our findings suggest a tumor-suppressive role for steroidal signaling by promoting postmitotic fate when local signaling is deteriorated.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to human clinical studies (Chen et al., 1998; Hendifar et al., 2009; Lin et al., 2012) mentioned in the Discussion.

claim: Reproduction triggers multiple physiological adaptations of organs such as liver, pancreas and gastrointestinal tract upon pregnancy in various species.
source: Reproduction is an energetically costly process triggering multiple physiological adaptations of organs such as liver, pancreas and gastrointestinal tract upon pregnancy in various species (Hammond, 1997; Roa and Tena-Sempere, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The female Drosophila melanogaster midgut is remodeled in size and physiology by stimulating intestinal stem cell (ISC) driven epithelial expansion upon mating to achieve an even energy balance.
source: As a part of the hormonal response to mating and increased metabolic energy consumption, the female Drosophila melanogaster midgut is remodeled in size and physiology by stimulating intestinal stem cell (ISC) driven epithelial expansion to achieve an even energy balance (Cognigni et al., 2011; Klepsatel et al., 2013; Reiff et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Local signaling pathways such as Notch (N), Jak/Stat, EGFR, Wnt/wingless, Insulin-receptor, Hippo/Warts and Dpp-signaling contribute to intestinal homeostasis under physiological and challenged conditions like bacterial infections.
source: Since the discovery of adult intestinal stem cells (Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006), local signaling pathways such as Notch (N), Jak/Stat, EGFR, Wnt/wingless, Insulin-receptor, Hippo/Warts and Dpp-signaling were shown to contribute to intestinal homeostasis under physiological and challenged conditions like bacterial infections (Miguel-Aliaga et al., 2018)(and references therein).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The midgut epithelium is maintained by ISC giving rise to only two types of differentiated cells: enteroendocrine cells (EE) and absorptive enterocytes (EC).
source: The midgut epithelium is maintained by ISC giving rise to only two types of differentiated cells: enteroendocrine cells (EE) and absorptive enterocytes (EC) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A and citations to foundational studies.

claim: Pluripotent ISC are able to self-renew or divide asymmetrically into either committed EC precursor cells called enteroblasts (EB) or enteroendocrine precursor (EEP) cells.
source: Pluripotent ISC are able to self-renew or divide asymmetrically into either committed EC precursor cells called enteroblasts (EB) or enteroendocrine precursor (EEP) cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational studies (Chen et al., 2018; Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007).

claim: Nine out of ten ISC mitosis give rise to EB specified by N-activation in EB daughters.
source: Nine out of ten ISC mitosis give rise to EB specified by N-activation in EB daughters (Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational studies.

claim: Post-mitotic EB retain a certain degree of plasticity by delaying their terminal differentiation through mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET).
source: Post-mitotic EB retain a certain degree of plasticity by: (1) delaying their terminal differentiation through mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET) (Antonello et al., 2015a)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: EB can change their fate to EE upon loss of the transcription factor klu (klumpfuss).
source: (2) changing their fate to EE upon loss of the transcription factor klu (klumpfuss)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Korzelius et al., 2019; Reiff et al., 2019).

claim: EB can undergo apoptosis as an additional homeostatic mechanism.
source: (3) undergoing apoptosis as an additional homeostatic mechanism (Korzelius et al., 2019; Reiff et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: EcR encodes for three different splice variants: EcR.A, EcR.B1 and EcR.B2.
source: EcR encodes for three different splice variants: EcR.A, EcR.B1 and EcR.B2 (Cherbas et al., 2003; Talbot et al., 1993), which we detected by PCR in intestinal tissue with highest expression for EcR.B2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: EcR is expressed in ISC, EB and EC.
source: Using EcR antibodies detecting all splice variants, we found EcR in ISC (positive for the Notch ligand Delta+), EB (Notch responsive element, NRE-GFP+) and EC (Discs-large-1, Dlg-1+, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D''' and Figure 1A for an overview).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B-D.

claim: Mated females show increases of progenitor numbers and newly generated progeny in the R5 region of the PMG over virgin females after seven days of esgReDDM-tracing.
source: After seven days of esgReDDM-tracing, mated females (MF, Figure 1D) showed increases of progenitor numbers (Figure 1H) and newly generated progeny (EE+EC, Figure 1I) in the R5 region of the PMG over virgin females (VF, Figure 1C) confirming previous observations (Reiff et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1H and 1I.

claim: Reducing EcR-levels with RNAi in MF results in a reduction of ISC/EB numbers and newly generated progeny to levels comparable to VF controls.
source: Reducing EcR-levels with two different >EcR RNAi stocks in MF resulted in a reduction of ISC/EB numbers (Figure 1E,H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1L) and newly generated progeny (Figure 1E,I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1L) to levels comparable to VF controls (Figure 1C,H,I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E, H, I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1L.

claim: Expressing dominant-negative EcR.B2 isoforms or EcR-heterozygosity using EcRM554fs phenocopy >EcR RNAi.
source: Independent of EcR-abundance, we found that expressing dominant-negative EcR.B2 isoforms or EcR-heterozygosity using EcRM554fs, a well described loss-of-function (LOF) allele, phenocopy >EcR RNAi (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I–K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1I-K.

claim: Overexpression of wildtype EcR.B2 and pan-EcR using esgReDDM in VF does not induce progenitor numbers or increase in new EC.
source: To investigate whether EcR-levels affect progenitor behavior, we overexpressed wildtype EcR.B2 and pan-EcR using esgReDDM in VF. We found neither induction of progenitor numbers nor an increase in new EC (Figure 1F–I), suggesting that EcR-dependent proliferation and differentiation of progenitors might be limited by 20HE availability (Figure 1J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F-I.

claim: 20HE titers in ovaries and hemolymph are increased 48 hr after mating compared to virgin females.
source: Determining 20HE titers 48 hr after mating using enzyme immunoassays, we confirmed previous reports of mating dependent increases of ovarian 20HE titers (Figure 2A; Ameku and Niwa, 2016; Harshman et al., 1999) and observed a similar increase in the hemolymph (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and citations to previous studies.

claim: 20HE titers in the hemolymph of ovoD1 females are reduced around 40–50% compared to wild-type females.
source: 20HE titers in the hemolymph of ovoD1 females are reduced around 40–50% compared to wild-type females (Figure 2B,A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and 2A.

claim: 20HE titers in hemolymph and remnants of the ovaries are significantly increased upon mating of ovoD1 females.
source: Interestingly, 20HE titers in hemolymph and remnants of the ovaries are still significantly increased upon mating of ovoD1 females (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: 20HE levels in sterile esgReDDM/ovoD1 MF increase the number of progenitors and progeny.
source: Consequently, 20HE titers in sterile esgReDDM/ovoD1 MF increase the number of progenitors (Figure 2E) and progeny (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: Feeding control esgReDDM VF with 50 µg/ml RH5849 strongly induces ISC mitosis, reflected by a tenfold increase in newly generated progeny over mating induction.
source: Feeding control esgReDDM VF 50 µg/ml with RH5849, we traced intestinal progenitors with pharmacologically activated EcR-signaling for seven days. RH5849 strongly induces ISC mitosis, reflected by a tenfold increase in newly generated progeny over mating induction (Figure 2G–I,Q).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G-I and 2Q.

claim: RH5849 mediated EcR-activation leads to no accumulation of progenitors.
source: Interestingly, RH5849 mediated EcR-activation leads to no accumulation of progenitors (Figure 2P) as observed in oncogenic manipulations or disruptions of intestinal homeostasis, suggesting a role for EcR in both, proliferation and differentiation (Antonello et al., 2015a; Chen et al., 2016; Patel et al., 2015; Reiff et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2P and inference from comparison to other studies.

claim: Forced expression of >EcI using esgReDDM in VF leads to no increase in progenitor numbers and new EC.
source: After seven days, forced expression of >EcI using esgReDDM in VF lead to no increase in progenitor numbers and new EC, underlining that VF 20HE levels are low (Figure 2K,P,Q).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2K, P, Q.

claim: >EcI in MF leads to an increase of newly generated EC exceeding typical mating induction of MF controls by 4.8 fold.
source: Further supporting this hypothesis,>EcI in MF lead to an increase of newly generated EC exceeding typical mating induction of MF controls by 4.8 fold (Figure 2L,P,Q).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2L, P, Q.

claim: Blocking 20HE uptake by EcI-RNAi in MF abolished ecdysone induced tissue expansion to VF control levels.
source: Blocking 20HE uptake by EcI-RNAi in MF abolished ecdysone induced tissue expansion to VF control levels (Figure 2N,P,Q).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2N, P, Q.

claim: There is no change in EcI expression upon mating.
source: In addition, we tested a function of the EcI gene in mating induction, but found no change in EcI expression upon mating (Figure 2O).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2O.

claim: Srebp-activity increases 2.2 fold upon mating.
source: Confirming previous observations, Srebp-activity increases 2.2 fold upon mating (mean fluorescence intensity, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D; Reiff et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, D and citation to previous work.

claim: Using the Srebp-reporter to drive >EcR RNAi in MF results in reduced Srebp-activity comparable to VF controls.
source: Using the Srebp-reporter to drive >EcR RNAi in MF, we found reduced Srebp-activity comparable VF controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E–F,H)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E-F, H.

claim: Feeding VF with RH5849 induced Srebp-activity 2.4 fold.
source: whereas feeding VF with RH5849 induced Srebp-activity 2.4 fold (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G, H.

claim: Feeding flies with RH5849 and forced expression of EcI significantly induced lipid uptake over controls.
source: In accordance with Srebp-activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D,G), feeding flies with RH5849 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K) and forced expression of EcI (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L) significantly induced lipid uptake (Figure 2—figure supplement 1O) over controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I,J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I-L, O.

claim: 20HE pulses lead to direct binding of EcR to regulatory regions of early ecdysone response genes Ecdysone-induced protein 74A (Eip74EF) and Ecdysone-induced protein 75B (Eip75B).
source: During Drosophila development, 20HE pulses lead to direct binding of EcR to regulatory regions of early ecdysone response genes Ecdysone-induced protein 74A (Eip74EF) and Ecdysone-induced protein 75B (Eip75B, Figure 3A; Bernardo et al., 2014; Karim and Thummel, 1991; Segraves and Hogness, 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Signal for Kr-h1-A, but not Kr-h1-B, and for all isoforms of Eip74EF and Eip75B was found by conventional PCR.
source: First, we performed conventional PCR to analyze JH- and Ecdysone target gene expression. Signal for Kr-h1-A (Kr-h1 in the following), but not Kr-h1-B, and for all isoforms of Eip74EF and Eip75B was found (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Eip74EF expression is unchanged upon mating.
source: To our surprise, we found Eip74EF expression unchanged, in contrast to its prominent role in the control of germline stem cell (GSC) proliferation in oogenesis (Ables and Drummond-Barbosa, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data (Figure 3C) and comparison to previous literature.

claim: Mating induces Eip75B-A and -C isoforms.
source: Instead, we found induction of Eip75B-A and -C isoforms (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Eip75B encodes for three protein isoforms (Eip75B-A, -B and –C) that differ in their N-terminal domain structure.
source: Eip75B encodes for three protein isoforms (Eip75B-A, -B and –C) that differ in their N-terminal domain structure (Segraves and Hogness, 1990)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Eip75B-B lacks one of the two zinc-finger DNA binding domains rendering it incapable of direct DNA binding.
source: and Eip75B-B lacks one of the two zinc-finger DNA binding domains rendering it incapable of direct DNA binding (White et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Reducing Eip75B levels with RNAi results in a significant increase in ISC and EB numbers but not in EC generation compared to VF controls.
source: Reducing Eip75B levels with RNAi, we found a significant increase in ISC and EB numbers (Figure 3D,E,L), but not in EC generation compared to VF controls (Figure 3M).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D, E, L, M.

claim: In MF, Eip75B knockdown reduced newly generated EC compared to MF controls.
source: In MF, Eip75B knockdown reduced newly generated EC compared to MF controls, pointing to a role of Eip75B in EB differentiation downstream of EcR-activation (Figure 3E,M).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E, M.

claim: Feeding flies with RH5849 lacking Eip75B in their intestinal progenitors did not result in newly generated progeny.
source: Interestingly, feeding flies with RH5849 lacking Eip75B in their intestinal progenitors (Figure 3F) did not result in newly generated progeny (Figure 3M compare to Figure 2Q), suggesting a central role for Eip75B in the RH5849 response.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F, M and comparison to Figure 2Q.

claim: MARCM clones of Eip75B-A (Eip75BA81) are significantly larger compared to controls.
source: MARCM clones of Eip75B-A (Eip75BA81) are significantly larger compared to controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D; Lee and Luo, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: Eip75BA81 deficient clones contain few differentiated EC.
source: Eip75BA81 deficient clones contain few differentiated EC (GFP+/Dlg-1+, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) suggesting disturbed EB to EC differentiation as observed for esgReDDM >Eip75 B-RNAi (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and comparison to Figure 3E.

claim: Forced expression of Eip75B-A and Eip75B-C strongly drive differentiation into EC depleting the entire progenitor pool.
source: Forced expression of Eip75B variants with esgReDDM resulted in three prominent phenotypes: (1) Eip75B-A and Eip75B-C strongly drive differentiation into EC (Dlg-1+, Figure 3G,J,M) depleting the entire progenitor pool (Figure 3G,J,M).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G, J, M.

claim: The Eip75B-B isoform induces ISC proliferation in VF and raises progenitor numbers suggesting slowed down but not inhibited terminal differentiation.
source: (2) The Eip75B-B isoform induces ISC proliferation in VF (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F) and raised progenitor numbers suggesting slowed down but not inhibited terminal differentiation (Figure 3I,L,M).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I, L, M and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: All Eip75B manipulations strongly reduce the number of newly differentiated EE.
source: (3) All Eip75B manipulations strongly reduce the number of newly differentiated EE (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Eip75B-A and Eip75B-C are sufficient to instantaneously drive progenitors into EC differentiation even in the absence of 20HE import.
source: Eip75B-A and Eip75B-C are sufficient to instantaneously drive progenitors into EC differentiation (Figure 3G,H,J,K) even in the absence of 20HE import (Figure 3H,K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G, H, J, K.

claim: Eip75B is a long term predicted PPARγ-homologue (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma) in Drosophila.
source: Eip75B is a long term predicted PPARγ-homologue (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma) in Drosophila.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: A close functional homology between Eip75B and PPARγ was recently confirmed in pharmacogenetic approaches demonstrating that Eip75B-mutant flies are irresponsive to PPARγ activating drugs.
source: A close functional homology got recently confirmed in pharmacogenetic approaches demonstrating that Eip75B-mutant flies are irresponsive to PPARγ activating drugs (Joardar et al., 2015; King-Jones and Thummel, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Human PPARγ plays a role in pregnancy related adaptations of lipid metabolism.
source: This homology is of particular interest, as human PPARγ plays a role in i) pregnancy related adaptations of lipid metabolism (Waite et al., 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Human PPARγ plays a role as target in colorectal cancer (CRC).
source: and ii) as target in colorectal cancer (CRC) (Sarraf et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Flies fed with food containing Pioglitazone show a strong increase in the number of progenitor cells and newly generated EC compared to controls.
source: Flies fed with food containing Pioglitazone show a strong increase in the number of progenitor cells (Figure 4B,E) and newly generated EC (Figure 4F) compared to controls (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, B, E, F.

claim: Knockdown of Eip75B led to irresponsiveness to Pioglitazone.
source: Strikingly, knockdown of Eip75B led to irresponsiveness to Pioglitazone (Figure 4C,D,F) suggesting that Pioglitazone activates Eip75B in intestinal progenitors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C, D, F.

claim: No changes in EB fate decisions towards EE differentiation were observed upon knockdown of EcR and Eip75B using kluReDDM.
source: No changes in EB fate decisions towards EE differentiation were observed upon knockdown of EcR and Eip75B (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B-D.

claim: Eip75B-A and Eip75B-C expression with kluReDDM phenocopied EB to EC differentiation effects observed in esgReDDM without non-autonomously inducing proliferation in wild-type ISC of VF and MF.
source: Eip75B-A and Eip75B-C expression with kluReDDM phenocopied EB to EC differentiation effects observed in esgReDDM (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G,I,J,K) without non-autonomously inducing proliferation in wild-type ISC of VF and MF (Figure 3—figure supplement 2J,K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G, I, J, K.

claim: Expressing Eip75B-B in kluReDDM leads to delayed EB differentiation similar to esgReDDM and non-autonomous induction of ISC mitosis.
source: Expressing Eip75B-B in kluReDDM lead to delayed EB differentiation similar to esgReDDM and non-autonomous induction of ISC mitosis (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2J,L; Patel et al., 2015; Reiff et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I and Figure 3—figure supplement 2J, L, and citations.

claim: Forced >Kr h1 expression doubles progenitor numbers in VF.
source: In VF lacking mating induction of both hormones (Figure 2A–C; Ameku and Niwa, 2016; Harshman et al., 1999; Reiff et al., 2015), forced >Kr h1 expression doubles progenitor numbers reproducing previous results (Figure 5B,I; Reiff et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B, I and citation to previous work.

claim: Forced Kr-h1-expression and simultaneous Eip75B-RNAi in MF increases progenitor numbers with only few newly generated EC.
source: However, we were able to analyze midguts of MF with forced Kr-h1-expression and simultaneous Eip75B-RNAi (Figure 5C,D), which increases progenitor numbers (Figure 5I) with only few newly generated EC (Figure 5J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, D, I, J.

claim: Simultaneous double knockdown of >Kr-h1-RNAi/Eip75B-RNAi in MF did not show mating induction with reduced progenitor numbers and differentiated progeny.
source: Simultaneous double knockdown of >Kr-h1-RNAi/Eip75B-RNAi (Figure 5H) in MF did not show mating induction. Progenitor numbers and differentiated progeny are reduced (Figure 5I,J) phenocopying single >Kr h1-RNAi (Reiff et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H, I, J and citation.

claim: A strong increase of progenitor numbers was observed forcing Kr-h1 and Eip75B-B expression.
source: Surprisingly, we observed a strong increase of progenitor numbers forcing Kr-h1 and Eip75B-B expression (Figure 5F,I,J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F, I, J.

claim: Eip75B-A and –C, despite raised Kr-h1-levels, drive progenitors into EC differentiation largely phenocopying sole Eip75B-A and -C expression.
source: Most interestingly, Eip75B-A and –C, despite of raised Kr-h1-levels, drive progenitors into EC differentiation largely phenocopying sole Eip75B-A and -C expression (compare Figures 3G,J and 5E,G,I,J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3G, J and 5E, G, I, J.

claim: In the Drosophila and mammalian intestinal stem cell niche, N-signaling specifies EE and EC fate.
source: In the Drosophila and mammalian intestinal stem cell niche, N-signaling specifies EE and EC fate (Jensen et al., 2000; Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007; VanDussen et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In Drosophila, mitosis of N mutant ISC generates only ISC-like progenitor cells and EE, which results in an intestinal epithelium accumulating a lack of newly produced EC and compensatory proliferation.
source: In Drosophila, mitosis of N mutant ISC generates only ISC-like progenitor cells and EE, which results in an intestinal epithelium accumulating a lack of newly produced EC and compensatory proliferation (Figure 6A,B; Chen et al., 2018; Guo and Ohlstein, 2015; Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007; Patel et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and reference to Figure 6A, B.

claim: Co-expression of Eip75B-A /- C with N-LOF strongly reduced total tumor number and smaller class I, II and III tumors.
source: Co-expression of Eip75B-A /- C with N-LOF strongly reduced total tumor number (Figure 6C,D,F) and smaller class I, II and III tumors (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C, D, F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Eip75B-RNAi results in confluent class IV tumors all along the PMG.
source: whereas Eip75B-RNAi results in confluent class IV tumors all along the PMG (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Eip75B-A and Eip75B-C re-enable EC differentiation despite the lack of N.
source: Since Eip75B-A and Eip75B-C re-enable EC differentiation despite the lack of N (Figure 6C,D; Dlg-1+/RFP+), we investigated whether the EcR-pathway and pharmacological Eip75B-activation are able to trigger EC fate in a N-LOF context.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C, D.

claim: Activation of Eip75B using Pioglitazone led to more newly generated EC compared to controls in N-LOF context.
source: Activation of Eip75B using Pioglitazone led to more newly generated EC (Figure 6H,I) compared to controls (Figure 6G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G, H, I.

claim: A slight, but significant reduction in the number of N-tumors was observed upon feeding Pioglitazone.
source: In addition, we observed a slight, but significant reduction in the number of N-tumors upon feeding Pioglitazone (Figure 6J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: Activating EcR-signaling with RH5849 or by raising intracellular levels of 20HE expressing > EcI in esgReDDM resulted in numerous confluent tumors.
source: We activated EcR-signaling with RH5849 (Figure 7B) or by raising intracellular levels of 20HE expressing > EcI in esgReDDM(Figure 7D). Either manipulation resulted in numerous confluent tumors reflecting the previously observed role of 20HE in proliferation (Figure 7F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B, D, F.

claim: >EcI RNAi- and >EcR RNAi significantly reduced tumor burden.
source: In line with this,>EcI RNAi- and >EcR RNAi significantly reduced tumor burden (Figure 7C,E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C, E, F.

claim: Activating 20HE signaling in N clones led to a tenfold increase in EC numbers over controls.
source: In agreement with our previous observations, activating 20HE signaling in N clones led to a tenfold increase in EC numbers over controls (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Forced expression of > E75 A/-C leads to instant EC formation.
source: and forced expression of > E75 A/-C to instant EC formation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: In the presence of N, its activity is increased upon RH5849 feeding.
source: Interestingly, in the presence of N, its activity is increased upon RH5849 feeding (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F), which suggests an interplay between Notch and EcR-signaling that might converge on Eip75B (this study) and klu (Korzelius et al., 2019; Reiff et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Drosophila melanogaster uses a classical r-selected reproductive strategy with high number of offspring and minimal parental care.
source: Drosophila melanogaster uses a classical r-selected reproductive strategy with high number of offspring and minimal parental care (Pianka, 1970).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Upon mating, egg production is increased tenfold supported by metabolic and behavioral adaptations such as food intake and transit, nutrient preference and a net increase of absorptive tissue in the PMG depending on JH release.
source: Upon mating, egg production is increased tenfold supported by metabolic and behavioral adaptations such as food intake and transit, nutrient preference and a net increase of absorptive tissue in the PMG depending on JH release (Carvalho et al., 2006; Cognigni et al., 2011; Reiff et al., 2015; Ribeiro and Dickson, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mating induces ovarian ecdysteroid biosynthesis stimulating egg production by ovarian GSC.
source: We confirmed that mating induces ovarian ecdysteroid biosynthesis stimulating egg production by ovarian GSC (Figure 2A; Ables and Drummond-Barbosa, 2010; Ameku and Niwa, 2016; Ameku et al., 2017; Harshman et al., 1999; König et al., 2011; Morris and Spradling, 2012; Uyehara and McKay, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 2A and citations to previous literature.

claim: The ovary is the only source for 20HE in adult females according to a study investigating the ecdysoneless mutants.
source: As a study investigating the ecdysoneless mutants suggested that the ovary is the only source for 20HE in adult females (Garen et al., 1977), we sought to diminish 20HE titers in adult females.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Genetic ablation of ovarian ecdysteroidogenic enzymes resulted in a reduction of mitotic ISC.
source: While this work was in review, genetic ablation of ovarian ecdysteroidogenic enzymes was performed in female flies and resulted in a reduction of mitotic ISC. However, a direct assessment of 20HE titers was not performed and a mating dependent context was not analyzed (Ahmed et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: Eip75B activates egg production in ovarian GSC.
source: Downstream of the EcR, we found differential regulation of Eip75B isoforms upon mating. Eip75B activates egg production in ovarian GSC (Ables and Drummond-Barbosa, 2010; König et al., 2011; Morris and Spradling, 2012; Uyehara and McKay, 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Knockdown of Eip75B reduces germarial size and number.
source: and its knockdown reduces germarial size and number.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Ables and Drummond-Barbosa, 2010; Morris and Spradling, 2012).

claim: Eip75B-B expression is at the lower detection limit and unchanged upon mating.
source: In our study, we dissected specific roles for Eip75B isoforms. Eip75B-B expression is at the lower detection limit (Figure 3B) and unchanged upon mating (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: Eip75B-B mutants are viable and fertile.
source: Eip75B-B mutants are viable and fertile
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Eip75B-B is interacting with DNA only upon forming heterodimers with Hormone receptor 3 (Hr3) temporarily repressing gene expression.
source: and Eip75B-B is interacting with DNA only upon forming heterodimers with Hormone receptor 3 (Hr3) temporarily repressing gene expression (Bialecki et al., 2002; Sullivan and Thummel, 2003; White et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Larval epidermis from Manduca sexta exposed to heightened JH-levels is sensitized to 20HE, which results in a 10-fold increase of Eip75B-A, but not of Eip75B-B expression.
source: This idea is supported by the finding that larval epidermis from Manduca sexta exposed to heightened JH-levels is sensitized to 20HE, which results in a 10-fold increase of Eip75B-A, but not of Eip75B-B expression (Dubrovskaya et al., 2004; Zhou et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: An in silico analysis of 4 kb regulatory regions upstream of Kr-h1 using JASPAR revealed several EcR/USP and Met consensus sequences.
source: An in silico analysis of 4 kb regulatory regions upstream of Kr-h1 using JASPAR revealed several EcR/USP and Met consensus sequences (Khan et al., 2018), suggesting that both hormonal inputs may also converge on Kr-h1 driving ISC proliferation (Figure 5B; Reiff et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis using JASPAR and inference about potential regulation.

claim: Upon EcR activation, Eip75B-A /- C promote EB to EC differentiation.
source: A key discovery of our study is that systemic 20HE directs local intestinal progenitor differentiation. Upon EcR activation, we found Eip75B-A /- C promoting EB to EC differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data throughout Figures 3-7.

claim: Detached EB acquire motility and are able to postpone their terminal epithelial integration after initial specification.
source: When tissue demand arises, EB are thought to physically separate from ISC and become independent of N. Detached EB acquire motility and are able to postpone their terminal epithelial integration after initial specification (Antonello et al., 2015a; Antonello et al., 2015b; Martin et al., 2018; Siudeja et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Nubbin (nub) mediated downregulation of esg and the nub-RB isoform is sufficient to initiate EC formation downstream of Notch signaling.
source: Epithelial integration of progenitors can be initiated experimentally by nubbin (nub) mediated downregulation of esg and the nub-RB isoform is sufficient to initiate EC formation downstream of Notch signaling (Korzelius et al., 2014; Tang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: EB-specific knockdown of Eip75B stalls their differentiation using kluReDDM.
source: This idea is supported by several lines of evidence: i) EB-specific knockdown of Eip75B stalls their differentiation using kluReDDM (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E), suggesting Eip75B functions after initial N-input.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: klu+-EB do not change fate upon Eip75B knockdown, suggesting a more mature EB differentiation status that already lost plasticity.
source: ii) klu+-EB do not change fate upon Eip75B knockdown, suggesting a more mature EB differentiation status that already lost plasticity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D; Korzelius et al., 2019; Reiff et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-D and inference.

claim: Forced Eip75B-A /- C expression in EB leads to their immediate differentiation independent of N-input.
source: iii) Forced Eip75B-A /- C expression in EB leads to their immediate differentiation independent of N-input (Figure 6C,D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C, D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, E.

claim: Eip75B was found to be highly expressed in EB in a recent study from the Perrimon lab.
source: In addition, Eip75B was found to be highly expressed in EB in a recent study from the Perrimon lab (Hung et al., 2018), raising the question about its transcriptional regulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: A plethora of studies established Eip75B as an early response gene downstream of the Ecdysone pathway.
source: A plethora of studies established Eip75B as an early response gene downstream of the Ecdysone pathway (Ables and Drummond-Barbosa, 2010; König et al., 2011; Morris and Spradling, 2012; Thummel, 1996; Uyehara and McKay, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: N activation leads to immediate EC differentiation of progenitors and thus phenocopies Eip75B-A /- C expression.
source: Another pathway stimulating Eip75B expression in EB might be the N pathway. N activation leads to immediate EC differentiation of progenitors and thus phenocopies Eip75B-A /- C expression (Hudry et al., 2016; Reiff et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and inference from phenotypic similarity.

claim: 20HE- and Notch-signaling have been shown to converge on target genes in various tissues and functions.
source: Indeed, 20HE- and Notch-signaling have been shown to converge on target genes in various tissues and functions (Mitchell et al., 2013; Sun et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both 20HE and Notch pathways acetylate H3K56 modifying multiple regulatory genomic regions including Eip75B.
source: and both pathways acetylate H3K56 modifying multiple regulatory genomic regions including Eip75B (Skalska et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Decreased PPARγ levels are associated with development of insulin resistance and failure of lipolysis in obese pregnant women.
source: Decreased PPARγ levels are associated with development of insulin resistance and failure of lipolysis in obese pregnant women (Rodriguez-Cuenca et al., 2012; Vivas et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PPARγ loss-of-function mutations are observed in around 8% of CRC patients.
source: In CRC, PPARγ loss-of-function mutations are observed in around 8% of patients (Sarraf et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: PPARγ expression correlates with good prognosis and PPARγ is epigenetically silenced during CRC progression.
source: PPARγ expression correlates with good prognosis and PPARγ is epigenetically silenced during CRC progression (Ogino et al., 2009; Pancione et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In vitro studies identified PPARγ promoting differentiation in various colon cancer cell lines.
source: In agreement with our in vivo experiments on Eip75B-A /- C in EB differentiation (Figures 3–7), in vitro studies identified PPARγ promoting differentiation in various colon cancer cell lines (Cesario et al., 2006; Shimizu and Moriwaki, 2008; Yamazaki et al., 2007; Yoshizumi et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In a CRC mouse model, biallelic loss of PPARγ leads to a 4-fold increase tumor incidence and reduced survival in female mice over males (ApcMin/+/PPARγ-/-).
source: In a CRC mouse model, biallelic loss of PPARγ leads to a 4-fold increase tumor incidence and reduced survival in female mice over males (ApcMin/+/PPARγ-/-) (McAlpine et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Males develop around three times more colon tumors with wild type PPARγ.
source: whereas males develop around three times more colon tumors with wild type PPARγ (Cooper et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Ovariectomized ApcMin/+ mice develop significantly more tumors and have decreased PPARγ expression.
source: In line with this, ovariectomized ApcMin/+ mice develop significantly more tumors and have decreased PPARγ expression, highlighting a possible link between PPARγ and estrogen signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from previous literature.

claim: Meta-analyses of hormone replacement studies have shown that estrogen confers a lower risk to develop CRC and better survival rates for female CRC patients.
source: Meta-analyses of hormone replacement studies have shown that estrogen confers a lower risk to develop CRC and better survival rates for female CRC patients (Chen et al., 1998; Hendifar et al., 2009; Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Human estradiol and 20HE activate the EcR with similar affinity and elicit Eip75B transcription by binding to EcRE (Ecdysone-Responsive Elements).
source: Indeed, human estradiol and 20HE activate the EcR with similar affinity and elicit Eip75B transcription by binding to EcRE (Ecdysone-Responsive Elements).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Martinez et al., 1991; Schwedes et al., 2011).

claim: EcRE can be converted to functional ERE (estrogen responsive elements) by a simple change of nucleotide spacing suggesting high conservation.
source: EcRE can be converted to functional ERE (estrogen responsive elements) by a simple change of nucleotide spacing suggesting high conservation (Martinez et al., 1991; Schwedes et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mating induced steroid hormone release signals to adjacent intestinal stem cells and controls their proliferation and differentiation of committed precursor cells through Eip75B/PPARγ.
source: Taken together, our findings reveal that mating induced steroid hormone release, which signals to adjacent intestinal stem cells, controls their proliferation and, more importantly, differentiation of committed precursor cells through Eip75B/PPARγ.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Ecdysone control of cell fate ensures the production of absorptive enterocytes during mating related intestinal adaptations and induces enterocyte fate in a Drosophila intestinal tumor model marked by loss of enterocyte differentiation.
source: Ecdysone control of cell fate ensures the production of absorptive enterocytes during mating related intestinal adaptations and induces enterocyte fate in a Drosophila intestinal tumor model marked by loss of enterocyte differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Eip75B/PPARγ exerts an anti-neoplastic role by promoting progenitor differentiation into postmitotic enterocyte fate, thereby reducing the pool of mitotically active cells.
source: Mechanistically, we propose that Eip75B/PPARγ exerts an anti-neoplastic role by promoting progenitor differentiation into postmitotic enterocyte fate, thereby reducing the pool of mitotically active cells.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the experimental data in Figures 6-7.

claim: Downstream of steroidal signaling, Eip75B/PPARγ promotes postmitotic cell fate when local signaling is deteriorated and thus might reflect a promising target for future studies in colorectal cancer models.
source: Downstream of steroidal signaling, Eip75B/PPARγ promotes postmitotic cell fate when local signaling is deteriorated and thus might reflect a promising target for future studies in colorectal cancer models.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future research directions based on the findings.
